To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

radio AGNs show a statistically significant excess in the number of satellite galaxies within 100 kpcs and that the incidence of AGN fueling depends primarilyon conditions in the host galaxy, not the parent cluster.

(1) radio AGNs are more likely to have satellites in their vicinity and that this is a function of the AGN excitation state; (2) radio AGNs have no detectable impact on the star formation in their satellite galaxies; (3) radio AGNs may be more likely to occur in massive galaxies in the field than in massive galaxies in clusters; and (4) AGN excitation is a function of host halo mass, not parent cluster mass.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of galaxies and the formation and evolution of stars and star clusters.
the study of the evolution of galaxies and the intergalactic medium (IGM), and how they interact.
the study of the effects of radio AGN on the properties of galaxies in their vicinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AGN feedback is not efficient in the local Universe.
the radio jets do not seem to have a significant impact on the star formation in their vicinity, neither by quenching nor by inducing star formation.
the satellites of radio AGNs are not different from the satellites of radio-quiet AGNs, but the hosts of the radio AGNs are.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radio AGN triggering and feedback are not directly related to the environment, and that they are not directly related with the satellite galaxies.
radio AGN do not appear to trigger star formation in their satellite galaxies, but the excess satellites themselves may be responsible for fueling the radio AGN.
radio AGN do not have an effect on the satellite properties of their hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radio AGN are not triggered by the presence of a large number of satellites, nor do radio AGN have an effect on their satellites.

the triggering of radio-loud AGN is more likely to be associated with the properties of the potential hosts (e.g., their halo masses and hot gas content) than with the properties of their parent cluster halos.
the radio AGN phenomenon is not a cluster phenomenon, but is a halo phenomenon.
